ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure there is an ethoxy fragment labeled EtO, with a negative sign drawn on the oxygen; on the right side there is an H–OEt fragment, corresponding to neutral ethanol. The middle main body is a fused-ring skeleton: the left side is a six-membered ring containing one C=C double bond, and the right side is fused with a five-membered ring; the upper bridgehead carbon of the five-membered ring is connected to a CN substituent, and the adjacent carbon on the right forms an exocyclic imine-like C=N connection with NH. There are also multiple curved arrows in the figure, but the question requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning: After ignoring all curved arrows, only the actual atoms, bonds, and charges are encoded. The left EtO− is converted to the ethoxide anion SMILES: CC[O-]. The right H–OEt is ethanol, SMILES: CCO. The middle fused-ring structure is encoded according to the fused ring, nitrile substituent, and exocyclic C(=N) imine as: N#CC1C(=N)CC2CC=CCC21. Connect the three unconnected components with dots, and write them in the specified order as CCO.CC[O-].N#CC1C(=N)CC2CC=CCC21.

method.method_draft: First ignore every curved arrow as instructed and treat only atoms, bonds, charges, and labels as structural information. Convert the left EtO− fragment to CC[O-] and the right H–OEt fragment to ethanol CCO. Then encode the central structure: a fused cyclohexene/cyclopentane ring system with a nitrile substituent on the bridge carbon and an exocyclic imine at the adjacent ring carbon, giving N#CC1C(=N)CC2CC=CCC21. Combine the disconnected components with dots, in the answer order: CCO.CC[O-].N#CC1C(=N)CC2CC=CCC21.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中左侧有一个标为 EtO 的乙氧基片段，氧上画有负号；右侧有一个 H–OEt 片段，对应中性乙醇。中间主体是一个并环骨架：左边为含一个 C=C 双键的六元环，右边与其稠合一个五元环；五元环上方桥位碳连有 CN 取代基，右侧相邻碳与 NH 形成外消旋/外环亚胺样的 C=N 连接。图中还有多条弯箭头，但题目要求忽略箭头。推理：忽略所有弯箭头后，只编码实际原子、键和电荷。左侧 EtO− 转为乙氧负离子 SMILES：CC[O-]。右侧 H–OEt 为乙醇，SMILES：CCO。中间并环结构按稠合环、腈基取代和外环 C(=N) 亚胺编码为：N#CC1C(=N)CC2CC=CCC21。将三个不相连组分用点号连接，并按指定顺序写为 CCO.CC[O-].N#CC1C(=N)CC2CC=CCC21。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Single direct transcription route: read the displayed transition-state diagram as a static molecular drawing, ignoring all curved arrows, then encode each disconnected component in SMILES. This is the natural and essentially unique solution path for this problem.
planner_metadata.image_role: Use the image to identify three disconnected chemical components: left ethoxide labeled EtO with a negative charge, right ethanol/protonated ethoxy fragment shown as H–OEt, and the central fused bicyclic molecule bearing a nitrile substituent labeled CN and an exocyclic imine C=NH on the five-membered ring. Also read the central ring framework as a fused cyclohexene/cyclopentane system with one C=C bond in the six-membered ring.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to know the task is to choose/write the SMILES for the transition-state structure and, crucially, to ignore the arrows; no additional textual chemical data are supplied.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply chemical drawing conventions: Et means ethyl (CC), OEt means ethoxy/ethanol connectivity through oxygen, a circled minus on EtO means ethoxide CC[O-], CN attached through carbon is nitrile C#N, and C=NH is encoded as an imine C=N in SMILES. Use dot notation for disconnected species and SMILES ring-closure numbering for the fused bicyclic skeleton.
